about: The Preface of the Most Holy Trinity. It confesses one God in three Persons, without confusion of Persons or division of substance, and leads into the common song with the choirs of angels.

seg.nr: Then the priest separates his hands and holds them apart until the end of the Preface. When it is finished, he joins them again and, bowing, says: Sanctus.

seg.tr: Truly it is right and just, fitting and leading to salvation, that we should give You thanks always and everywhere:

a.g: always and everywhere give thanks to You

seg.tr: O Lord, holy Father, almighty eternal God:
You, with Your only-begotten Son and the Holy Spirit, are one God and one Lord: not in the oneness of a single Person, but in the Trinity of one substance.
For what we believe of Your glory through Your revelation, we understand likewise of Your Son and of the Holy Spirit, without making any distinction.

ex.w064: ‘Sine differentia discretionis’ concerns what we profess about the glory of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit: the same glory belongs to all three Persons. It does not erase their personal distinctions, which the next sentence explicitly affirms.

seg.tr: So that, in the confession of the true and eternal Godhead, distinction in Persons, unity in essence, and equality in majesty may be adored.

a.g: of the true and eternal Godhead
equality in majesty may be adored

seg.tr: Which the Angels and Archangels, the Cherubim also and the Seraphim, praise; they do not cease daily to cry out with one voice, saying:

a.g: the Angels and Archangels, and also the Cherubim and Seraphim, praise

ex.w085: Quam links this praise to what precedes. It may refer to the equality in majesty just mentioned or to the earlier Godhead: both aequalitas and Deitas are feminine nouns.
